datapoints.unit: deliveries per hour worked (trip + on-call time), e-bike workers
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (Table 3)
datapoints.verbatim: Table 3. App Delivery Workers, Hours, and Deliveries, by Mode of Transportation, NYC, Fourth Quarter 2021 ... E-bike 46.1 [% workers] 54.1 [% hours] 65.8 [% deliveries] 21.3 [hours per week] 2.030 [deliveries per hour]; Non-Car 56.1 69.4 77.7 22.2 1.869; Walking ... 25.7 1.266; Motorcycle ... 25.2 1.530; Car 43.9 30.6 22.4 17.5 1.128
datapoints.notes: Record-level app data (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Relay). Denominator includes on-call time; workers were 61% engaged/39% on-call, so per trip-hour e-bike rate is ~3.3. Pre-minimum-pay-rule; 'e-bike' includes misreported mopeds.

datapoints.unit: deliveries per hour (trip + on-call hours), all modes, weekly average
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, Restaurant Delivery App Data: October-December 2024 (Table 1)
datapoints.verbatim: Deliveries per hour 1.42 [Q4 2023] 2.53 [Q4 2024] 1.11 78 [% change] ... Total deliveries (in millions) 2.67 2.72 ... Trip hours (in thousands) 861 888 ... On-call hours (in thousands) 1,017 186 ... Total hours (in thousands) 1,879 1,074
datapoints.notes: Post-minimum-pay: apps cut on-call time 82%, so deliveries per total hour jumped. Derived: deliveries per TRIP hour = 2.72M / 888k = 3.06. Hours are not de-duplicated for multi-apping (true per-hour rate slightly higher). Q1 2024 figure was 1.89 deliveries/hour (Restaurant Dive, https://www.restaurantdive.com/news/new-york-city-delivery-wage-gains-offset-job-cuts-city-says/721332/).

datapoints.unit: deliveries per hour worked (trip + on-call), car workers
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (Table 3)
datapoints.verbatim: Car 43.9 [% workers] 30.6 [% hours] 22.4 [% deliveries] 17.5 [hours per week] 1.128 [deliveries per hour] ... throughout the day, car drivers perform substantially fewer deliveries per hour than e-bike workers.
datapoints.notes: NYC car is a lower bound for LA (NYC car deliveries hampered by traffic/parking). Compare Gridwise national active-hour figures below (1.51-1.70 per ACTIVE hour, which excludes waiting time).

datapoints.unit: deliveries per active hour (on-order time only), median DoorDash driver
datapoints.source: Gridwise blog, How Much Do DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub Drivers Make (2025 data)
datapoints.verbatim: The median Uber Eats driver completes about 1.70 deliveries per hour, while DoorDash drivers only complete 1.51 deliveries per hour. The median Grubhub driver completes about 1.61 deliveries per hour. ... Active hours count only time spent on an order, so this figure excludes waiting time between deliveries.
datapoints.notes: Verbatim as returned by search summary spanning Gridwise DoorDash (https://gridwise.io/blog/how-much-do-doordash-drivers-make), Uber Eats (https://gridwise.io/blog/how-much-do-uber-eats-drivers-make) and Grubhub (https://gridwise.io/blog/how-much-do-grubhub-drivers-make) pages. Because active hours exclude waiting, per ONLINE hour is lower (~1.0-1.2 if ~60-70% engaged). Gridwise users skew to car drivers and heavier users. DoorDash gross $12.43 per active hour, $240/week average (2025).

datapoints.unit: completed offers per engaged hour (derived = 196,871 offers/wk / (15,489 accounts x 7.3 engaged hrs))
datapoints.source: Seattle Office of Labor Standards, SMC 8.37 Data Report (first report)
datapoints.verbatim: there was an average of 196,871 offers per week completed by the five largest companies. ... there were on average 15,489 engaged worker accounts per week. ... there was an average of 7.3 engaged hours per worker account per week. ... there was an average of 12.0 engaged + available hours per worker account per week. ... there was an average of 56.5% engaged time per week.
datapoints.notes: Derived ratio, not stated by OLS. Per ONLINE (engaged+available) hour: 196,871 / (15,489 x 12.0) = 1.06 offers/online hour (approximate; the 12.0 figure excludes the pre-scheduled-package company). Offers include grocery and some package work, and an offer may contain multiple drop-offs. Engaged time = acceptance to completion.

datapoints.unit: deliveries per full-time courier per day
datapoints.source: Derived from DCWP 2022 (2.03/hr e-bike), NYSERDA/C2SMART 2025 (hours/day), DCWP Q4 2024 (deliveries/worker-week)
datapoints.verbatim: As shown in Figure 11, most delivery workers work more than 5 days a week (86.2%) and at least 7 hours per day (73.7%). [NYSERDA 25-38, p.16, intercept survey n=331, late 2024/early 2025] ... Delivery workers made 2.72 million deliveries per week [DCWP Q4 2024; 60k workers performing trips -> 45.3 deliveries per trip-performing worker-week; 70k total worker accounts -> 38.9]
datapoints.notes: Derived: 7-10 hrs/day x 2.0-2.5 deliveries/hr (NYC e-bike, incl. on-call) = 14-25/day. NYC Q4 2024 average worker account (15.2 hrs/wk) does 38.9 deliveries/week; a full-time (30+ hr) NYC e-bike courier at 2.5-3.0/hr does 75-100/week. No LA self-report ('33 deliveries in DTLA shift' type) was verified in this pass - see gaps.

datapoints.value: offer every 4 min; accepted every 11 min on-call
datapoints.unit: minutes
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC
datapoints.verbatim: Workers spend 61% of their working time engaged in a trip and 39% on-call. During on-call time, they receive a trip offer every 4 minutes and accept an offer every 11 minutes, on average.
datapoints.notes: Useful for converting on-call to trips and for utilization assumptions.

datapoints.unit: hours per week on platform, average Dasher (Q4 2025)
datapoints.source: DoorDash 2025 Economic Impact Report as reported by Santa Monica Daily Press
datapoints.verbatim: Dashers averaged about four hours per week on the platform during the fourth quarter, with the typical Dasher active for roughly 10 weeks during the year. ... more than 8 million people dashed in the U.S. in 2025, collectively earning nearly $20 billion including tips. ... 85% of Dashers have other income sources or responsibilities
datapoints.notes: Company-reported via press. DoorDash 'Behind the Dash' (Jul 27, 2023) states 'The average Dasher spends less than 4 hours per week on delivery'. California Dashers 'spent an average of roughly six hours per week on delivery' in Q4 2023 (DoorDash Prop 22 post, May 17, 2024).

datapoints.unit: share of Dashers by average weekly hours (quarterly averages)
datapoints.source: DoorDash, Behind the Dash: Insights into the Flexibility and Freedom of Dashing
datapoints.verbatim: The average Dasher spends less than 4 hours per week on delivery ... 72% of Dashers average even less than that ... only a few highly active Dashers (the top 12%) average more than 10 hours per week ... 96% of all Dashers averaged less than 20 hours per week on delivery ... 19% dashed in only a single week over the quarter ... nearly 3 out of 4 (73%) did not dash in 4 or more weeks across the quarter
datapoints.notes: Company self-report, US-wide. Hours are 'on delivery' (engaged), averaged over all weeks in the quarter including zero weeks, which drags the mean down.

datapoints.unit: share of Dashers averaging 25+ hours/week
datapoints.source: Derived from DoorDash Behind the Dash (96% under 20 hours/week)
datapoints.verbatim: 96% of all Dashers averaged less than 20 hours per week on delivery
datapoints.notes: DoorDash does not publish a 25+ or 35+ hour share; 4% at 20+ hours is the bound. Berkeley (Gridwise sample, Jan 2022) found 12% of delivery drivers full-time (32+ hrs) but that sample skews to committed drivers. NYC survey found 46.6% of e-bike workers full-time (30+ hrs) - a very different, career workforce.

datapoints.unit: share of delivery drivers / share of delivery trips
datapoints.geography: Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, Chicago metros (pooled)
datapoints.source: UC Berkeley Labor Center, Gig Passenger and Delivery Driver Pay in Five Metro Areas (p.18)
datapoints.verbatim: Of the 30,100 trips in our non-DoorDash sample, full-time drivers (32 hours or more) accounted for 42 percent. Passenger drivers were more likely (26 percent) to work full time than delivery drivers (12 percent). As Figure 1 shows, full-time transportation drivers accounted for 49 percent of all passenger trips, while full-time delivery drivers accounted for 27 percent of delivery trips. ... those who work over 20 hours a week still account for 59 percent of the delivery trips in our data.
datapoints.notes: Gridwise-tracked drivers (~1,100 drivers, 52,000 trips) - car-based, skewed toward more engaged workers. Key for order-weighting: 59% of delivery trips done by 20+ hr/week drivers.

datapoints.unit: share of shift time / miles spent waiting between deliveries (P1)
datapoints.source: UC Berkeley Labor Center, Gig Passenger and Delivery Driver Pay in Five Metro Areas (Table 1)
datapoints.verbatim: Table 1. P1 times and miles for delivery and passenger drivers ... Delivery California 29.9 [mean % of shift time] 35.3 [median] 47.2 [mean % of shift miles] 46.2 [median] ... average P1 times are about 30 percent among delivery and passenger drivers. ... P2 time equals 13 percent of combined P2 and P3 time, as we found for delivery workers.
datapoints.notes: Gives engaged share ~65-70% for CA car couriers, consistent with ShiftTracker's 60-70% and Seattle's 56.5%.

datapoints.unit: average hours per week (trip + on-call), excluding weeks with no work
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP 2022 study; DCWP Restaurant Delivery App Data Q4 2024 (Table 1)
datapoints.verbatim: Weekly hours average 21.3 for e-bike workers, 17.5 for car drivers, and 20.7 overall. [2022 study] ... Average hours 17.3 [Q4 2023] 15.2 [Q4 2024] -2.1 -12 [Q4 2024 report, per worker account]
datapoints.notes: Q4 2024 hours are per app-account and fell mainly because on-call hours were cut 82% after the pay rule.

datapoints.unit: share of workers performing deliveries full-time (30+ hours/week)
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (Table 6)
datapoints.verbatim: Responses also indicate that 46.6% of e-bike workers and 34.9% of car drivers perform deliveries on a full-time basis. ... Full-time is defined as 30 or more hours per week. Part-time is defined as fewer than 30 hours per week. Source: Department analysis of data from the NYC Delivery Worker Survey.
datapoints.notes: Post-stratified survey of >8,000 workers. NYSERDA/C2SMART 2025 intercept survey (n=331, rest-hub sample skewed to full-timers): 86.2% work more than 5 days/week, 73.7% at least 7 hours/day.

datapoints.unit: engaged hours per engaged worker account per week (12.0 engaged + available hours)
datapoints.source: Seattle Office of Labor Standards, SMC 8.37 Data Report (pp.17-19)
datapoints.verbatim: For the period shown, there was an average of 7.3 engaged hours per worker account per week. From Half 1 2024 to Half 1 2025 ... increase in weekly engaged hours per worker from 7.4 hours to 7.5 hours (+2.0%). ... there was an average of 12.0 engaged + available hours per worker account per week ... decrease ... from 12.7 hours to 12.0 hours (-5.6%). ... there was an average of 56.5% engaged time per week.
datapoints.notes: Per worker ACCOUNT (worker-company pair); OLS notes this underestimates hours per unique worker because of multi-apping (12-14% of workers). Engaged time excludes available time under one hour between offers. Weekly earnings averaged $320.76 per account.

datapoints.unit: workers; ratios derived
datapoints.source: Seattle Office of Labor Standards, SMC 8.37 Data Report (pp.9-13)
datapoints.verbatim: there were on average 15,489 engaged worker accounts per week. From Half 1 2024 to Half 1 2025 ... increase in average weekly engaged workers accounts from 14,345 to 16,200 worker accounts (+12.9%). ... There was a total of 92,801 unique workers in the first eighteen months after the law became effective. Across all complete quarters shown, there was an average of 34,646 unique engaged workers per quarter. ... 60.4% of workers engaged in any given quarter of 2024 were engaged in the following quarter, on average. ... 9.2% of workers had not engaged in Quarter 1 2025 but had worked in previous quarters and returned ... in Quarter 2 2025.
datapoints.notes: Weekly figure is accounts (not deduplicated); with ~13% multi-app workers, unique weekly-active is roughly 15,489/1.13 = ~13,700, so weekly/quarterly unique is ~0.40 (0.45 unadjusted). Covers all app-based on-demand work (restaurant, grocery, some package), not just food.

datapoints.unit: workers; ratios derived
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (pp.5, 12)
datapoints.verbatim: The Department estimates that as of the second quarter of 2022, 61,000 delivery workers were working for restaurant apps in NYC in any given week. However, the total number of people working for the apps over longer time periods may be considerably higher. For instance, at the four largest apps, in the fourth quarter of 2021 there were 219,787 worker accounts associated with at least one delivery in NYC. After adjusting for multi-apping, the Department estimates that these accounts were held by 122,104 individuals ... In the fourth quarter of 2021, 39% of the unique worker phone numbers in the Department's data were associated with deliveries in two or fewer weeks.
datapoints.notes: Best available weekly-active to quarterly-active anchor for a food-delivery-only workforce: ~0.5. Q4 2024 DCWP: 70k total worker accounts/week and 60k performing trips (not deduplicated).

datapoints.unit: weekly-active / annual-active (derived: typical Dasher active ~10 of 52 weeks)
datapoints.source: DoorDash 2025 Economic Impact Report via Santa Monica Daily Press; DoorDash Behind the Dash 2023
datapoints.verbatim: the typical Dasher active for roughly 10 weeks during the year ... more than 8 million people dashed in the U.S. in 2025 [2025 EIR] ... 19% dashed in only a single week over the quarter ... 73% did not dash in 4 or more weeks across the quarter [Behind the Dash, 2023]
datapoints.notes: If 'typical' is the mean, average weekly-active Dashers ~ 8M x 10/52 = ~1.5M. The 2023 quarterly stats imply weekly-active/quarterly-active of roughly 0.25-0.30 for DoorDash (73% dash in fewer than 4 of 13 weeks). Contrast NYC (~0.5) and Seattle (~0.4-0.45).

datapoints.unit: daily-active / weekly-active couriers
datapoints.source: Derived from DoorDash hours distribution (4 hrs/wk avg, 72% under 4 hrs) and NYSERDA/C2SMART NYC survey (86.2% work >5 days/week)
datapoints.verbatim: most delivery workers work more than 5 days a week (86.2%) and at least 7 hours per day (73.7%) [NYSERDA 25-38, p.16] ... Dashers averaged about four hours per week on the platform during the fourth quarter [DoorDash 2025 EIR]
datapoints.notes: No source publishes a daily/weekly active ratio directly. Reasoning: a Dasher averaging ~4 hrs/week in 2-3 hr sessions works ~1.5-2.5 days/week -> 0.2-0.35 of weekly-active on a given day; NYC full-timers at 6+ days/week -> ~0.85. DCWP 2022 Figure 10 reports 'Workers engaged ... the daily average number of workers connected to an app' by time of day but only as a chart (not extractable as text) - see gaps. Blend for LA should weight by the share of orders done by heavy users (Berkeley: 59% of delivery trips by 20+ hr/week drivers).

datapoints.unit: share of delivery workers working for more than one app
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (pp.5, 17)
datapoints.verbatim: the Department finds that 56.3% of delivery workers work for more than one app and that 17.7% of working time is logged concurrently. ... 219,787 accounts ... were held by 122,104 unique individuals
datapoints.notes: Pre-minimum-pay; DCWP expects reduced multi-apping after the rule. Accounts-per-person ratio 1.80 in Q4 2021 is the de-duplication factor for summing app-reported worker counts.

datapoints.unit: share of unique engaged workers engaged on two or more large network companies in the same quarter (Q2 2025)
datapoints.source: Seattle Office of Labor Standards, SMC 8.37 Data Report (p.12)
datapoints.verbatim: the proportion of multi-apping workers grew from 10.8% in Quarter 1 2024 to 12.6% in Quarter 1 2025 (+1.8 percentage points). From Quarter 2 2024 to Quarter 2 2025, the proportion grew by a larger amount from 11.4% to 14.3% (+2.9 percentage points). ... More than 85% of the workers only worked on one app.
datapoints.notes: Matched on zip + phone digits across company datasets; quarterly window. Much lower than NYC's 56%, closer to Gridwise's national 24%.

datapoints.unit: share of gig workers who ran more than one platform in 2025
datapoints.source: Gridwise Analytics, Multi-Apping's Role in Pay and Platform Power
datapoints.verbatim: About 24.3% of gig workers ran more than one platform in 2025 ... Only 18% of DoorDash delivery drivers also work for Uber Eats ... Just 4% of DoorDash drivers use multiple apps including Uber, Grubhub, or Instacart
datapoints.notes: Includes rideshare; the 18% DoorDash-Uber Eats overlap is the most relevant de-dup factor for DoorDash + Uber Eats in a car-dominated market like LA. Data basis Jan-Dec 2024 Gridwise app users (sample size not disclosed).

datapoints.unit: share of drivers driving for more than one platform over a two-week period; 20% of delivery shifts used more than one app
datapoints.geography: LA, SF Bay, Seattle, Boston, Chicago metros
datapoints.source: UC Berkeley Labor Center, Gig Passenger and Delivery Driver Pay in Five Metro Areas (p.17)
datapoints.verbatim: In our full sample, including DoorDash, about 45 percent of drivers were multi-app drivers; that is, they drove for more than one platform over the two-week period. Using multiple apps in the same shift was less common. Passenger drivers used more than one app in 24 percent of their shifts; the comparable figure for delivery drivers was 20 percent. ... Relatively few drivers (11 percent) performed both sets of services over the two-week period.
datapoints.notes: Gridwise-tracked (multi-app-prone) sample; includes passenger drivers.

datapoints.unit: USD per hour while on deliveries (engaged), average LA Dasher, 2023
datapoints.source: DoorDash, Thanks to California's Prop 22 Dashers are Doing Better than Ever
datapoints.verbatim: Los Angeles Dashers earned around $35 per hour while on deliveries in 2023, a 39% increase from 2020 ... California Dashers earned around $36 per hour while on deliveries in 2023 on average ... California Dashers spent an average of roughly six hours per week on delivery
datapoints.notes: Company claim, engaged-time only (P2+P3), gross incl. tips, before expenses. Berkeley found company P3-based figures ~10% higher than independent P23 estimates; per online hour would be ~65-70% of this (~$23-25).

datapoints.unit: USD per active hour, LA DoorDash, 2026
datapoints.source: ShiftTracker, LA DoorDash Earnings 2026
datapoints.verbatim: LA Dashers typically gross $22-$30/hour during peak windows ... Weekend dinners $28-$36/hour ... Morning $14-$20/hour ... Afternoon dip $12-$18/hour ... In most of LA, you're looking at 2-5 miles between drop-off and next pickup ... Engaged time: 60-70% of total app-on time ... A driver online for 8 hours typically logs 5-5.5 hours of engaged time ... Full-time typically means 45-55 hours per week ... Full-time weekly gross typically lands at $900-$1,400 in 2026 ... $19.20/hour during engaged time in 2026 [Prop 22 floor] ... Miles per shift 80-150
datapoints.notes: Blog with no disclosed sample; ranges are plausible and consistent with Prop 22 floor ($19.20 engaged in 2026) but unverified. Useful for LA engaged-share (60-70%) and inter-order distance (2-5 mi).

datapoints.unit: USD gross per hour, all delivery platforms, Q4 2025 (NATIONAL - no LA-specific Gridwise figure found)
datapoints.geography: United States (Gridwise users); LA not disclosed
datapoints.source: Gridwise 2026 Annual Gig Mobility Report via Food On Demand; Gridwise DoorDash earnings page
datapoints.verbatim: Hourly delivery earnings rose 3.2 percent between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025, reaching $14.66 late last year. [Food On Demand summary of Gridwise report] ... The average DoorDash driver earned $12.43 gross per active hour in 2025 [Gridwise, https://gridwise.io/blog/how-much-do-doordash-drivers-make] ... Delivery tips: $4.16 in Q4 2025
datapoints.notes: Gridwise's public pages and the 2026 report landing page do not break out Los Angeles; the LA figure requires the full downloadable report (gap). Gridwise hourly = per active hour tracked in-app; much lower than DoorDash's $35 engaged-hour claim because of definitional differences and market mix.

datapoints.unit: deliveries per online hour, LA car courier
datapoints.source: Derived from Gridwise national DoorDash 1.51/active hour (2025), ShiftTracker LA $22-30/hr peak vs $5-8 base per delivery, NYC car 1.128/hr incl. on-call (2021)
datapoints.verbatim: DoorDash drivers only complete 1.51 deliveries per hour [active hour, Gridwise 2025] ... LA Dashers typically gross $22-$30/hour during peak windows [ShiftTracker 2026] ... Car 17.5 [hrs/wk] 1.128 [deliveries/hr] [NYC DCWP 2021]
datapoints.notes: No LA-specific deliveries-per-hour measurement was found. Peak LA gross of $22-30/hr at ~$10-13 gross per delivery incl. tip implies ~2-2.5/hr at peak; off-peak ~1.5. DoorDash 2026 two-wheel report: two-wheel Dashers 'earned on average over 10% more per hour spent on the app than those delivering by car' and 'spent around 15% less time traveling from offer acceptance to store arrival' (US+Canada, 2025; https://about.doordash.com/en-us/news/2026-two-wheel-report) - use as bike-vs-car productivity multiplier.

datapoints.unit: relative difference, two-wheel vs car Dashers
datapoints.source: DoorDash, New Report Demonstrates Two-Wheeled Devices Continue to Deliver for Local Commerce
datapoints.verbatim: Dashers in the U.S. and Canada on two-wheels earned on average over 10% more per hour spent on the app than those delivering by car ... such Dashers spent around 15% less time traveling from offer acceptance to store arrival for pickup ... The number of deliveries on two-wheeled devices grew nearly four times faster than car-based deliveries did across the U.S. and Canada between 2024 and 2025
datapoints.notes: Company claim; consistent with NYC DCWP e-bike 2.03 vs car 1.13 deliveries/hr (though NYC gap is far larger).

datapoints.unit: share of daily order volume in dinner daypart
datapoints.source: DoorDash internal data via Restaurant Dive (Jul 30, 2024)
datapoints.verbatim: Internal DoorDash data indicated order volumes in the lunch period were roughly half the order volumes of the dinner daypart, with a similar lull from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.
datapoints.notes: No verbatim dinner percentage published. A search summary cited 'Lunch delivery occasions grew to 19.2% of total delivery volume in the 52 weeks ending March 16, 2025' (attributed to Circana) but the source page could not be verified in this pass - treat as unverified. If lunch ~19% and dinner ~2x lunch, dinner ~38-40%; with late-night and afternoon lulls, 35-45% is the working range. NYC DCWP 2022 Figure 10: 'more delivery workers connect to the apps during peak dinner hours ... spend more of their time engaged in trips ... and perform more deliveries per hour' (chart only).

datapoints.value: Fridays and Saturdays; 6 pm most common order time
datapoints.unit: qualitative
datapoints.source: DoorDash, New Data from DoorDash Showcases Latest Trends in Food Delivery
datapoints.verbatim: DoorDash users tend to order food most often on Fridays and Saturdays after a long week of work, with orders spiking around dinnertime, with 6 pm as the overall most common time. [as summarized in search results]
datapoints.notes: No Fri-Sun share of weekly orders was found in any DoorDash trend report; gap. Berkeley: 'delivery drivers tend to drive during evening meal hours.'

datapoints.value: deliveries lower in summer, higher in winter
datapoints.unit: qualitative
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, Restaurant Delivery App Data Q4 2024 (Technical Note)
datapoints.verbatim: Throughout this report, comparisons are made between the same quarter year-over-year. This is done to control for seasonal impacts on the figures presented. The number of deliveries is generally lower in the summer and higher in the winter.
datapoints.notes: LA has milder seasonality; use as a caution that Q4 counts run above annual average.

datapoints.unit: share
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, A Minimum Pay Rate for App-Based Restaurant Delivery Workers in NYC (Table 3)
datapoints.verbatim: non-car modes of transportation account for 56% of workers but 69% of hours worked and 78% of deliveries. The difference in these distributions is explained by higher hours per week, and deliveries per hour worked for workers using a non-car mode of transportation.
datapoints.notes: Shows why a per-restaurant or per-order calibration on NYC must be adjusted for LA's car-dominated mode mix: car workers deliver 22% of orders with 44% of workers.

datapoints.unit: share of intercept-survey respondents
datapoints.source: NYSERDA / NYU C2SMART, New York City Delivery Workers: Insights on Travel Patterns and E-Mobility (pp.16-19)
datapoints.verbatim: The intercept survey collected a final tally of 331 responses, representing a response rate of approximately 38% of the delivery workers approached. ... most delivery workers work more than 5 days a week (86.2%) and at least 7 hours per day (73.7%). ... nearly half of all respondents used their own personal e-bike for deliveries (47.9%), followed by rental e-bikes (24.4%), gas mopeds (13.4%), e-mopeds (7.2%), pedal bikes (4.6%), and other modes (2.6%).
datapoints.notes: Intercept sample at rest hubs over-represents full-time and rental-e-bike workers (authors' caveat). Report does not give trips per day per worker or a multi-app share (checked full text).

datapoints.unit: weekly averages (not de-duplicated for multi-apping)
datapoints.source: NYC DCWP, Restaurant Delivery App Data: October-December 2024 (Table 1)
datapoints.verbatim: Total workers (in thousands) 109 [Q4 2023] 70 [Q4 2024] ... Workers performing trips (in thousands) 78 60 ... Total trips (in millions) 2.63 2.58 ... Total deliveries (in millions) 2.67 2.72 ... Statistics are not adjusted for multi-apping, and so the reported 'Employment' figures should not be used to determine the true (unduplicated) number of workers
datapoints.notes: Apps covered: DoorDash, FanTuan, Grubhub, HungryPanda, Uber Eats. Includes some grocery deliveries.

gaps: No published daily-active / weekly-active ratio for gig couriers from any platform, regulator, or academic source; the DCWP 2022 Figure 10 'daily average number of workers connected to an app' by hour exists only as a chart image (would need the figure data or a FOIL request).

DoorDash does not disclose monthly- or weekly-active Dasher counts (only '8M+ dashed in 2025', ~4 hrs/week, ~10 weeks/year); share dashing 25+/35+ hours per week is not published (only 96% under 20 hrs, 2023).

No Los Angeles-specific deliveries-per-hour or hours-per-week measurement found; Gridwise LA earnings/trips figures are only in the paid/downloadable 2026 report; Berkeley 2024 reports California-level, not LA-level, delivery figures in the text extracted.

No verbatim dinner-daypart share of orders or Fri-Sun share of weekly orders from DoorDash trend reports; only 'lunch roughly half of dinner' (2024) and qualitative Fri/Sat/6pm peak. The '19.2% lunch share (Circana, 52 wks to Mar 16 2025)' figure surfaced in search but its source page was not verified.
NYSERDA/C2SMART 2025 report gives hours/day and days/week distributions (Figure 10 chart; text gives 86.2% >5 days, 73.7% >=7 hrs/day) but not trips per day per worker or multi-app share.
DCWP quarterly reports after Q4 2024 (Q1 2025 - Q2 2026) were not located in search results; the latest verified quarter is Q4 2024 (2.53 deliveries/hr, 60k trip-performing accounts/week).
Uber Eats courier hours-per-week and Grubhub-specific hours data were not collected.
Rider self-reports (YouTube/TikTok 'X deliveries in DTLA shift') were not searched in this pass.
Seattle weekly unique (de-duplicated) worker count is not published; only weekly engaged worker accounts (15,489) and quarterly unique workers (34,646).
